158.h: 63 - Sahl ibn Ḥunayf Abū Thābit al-Anṣārī al-Awsī * (ع)
158.t:
al-ʿAwfī.
Father of Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl, and brother of ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf.
He witnessed Badr and the other battles.
Narrating from him: ابناه؛ أبو أمامة وعبد الله؛ وعبيد بن السباق، وأبو وائل، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، ويسير بن عمرو؛ وآخرون.
He was one of the commanders of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him).
He died in Kufa, in the year 38 AH, and ʿAlī prayed over him.
His hadith is in the Six Books (الكتب الستة) (2) . ⟦2:325⟧
al-Ḥākim, in his Mustadrak: via: عبد الواحد بن زياد، حدثنا عثمان بن حكيم، حدثتنا الرباب جدتي، عن سهل بن حنيف:
I bathed in a torrent and came out feverish, so the Prophet ﷺ said: “Command Abū Thābit to give charity (1)” .
مالك: عن ابن شهاب، عن أبي أمامة بن سهل، قال:
ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah saw Sahl ibn Ḥunayf and said: By Allah, I have never seen the like of today, not even the skin of a veiled maiden!
Then Sahl collapsed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was approached and told: O Messenger of Allah! Can you do something for Sahl? By Allah, he cannot lift his head.
He said: “Do you suspect anyone in this?”
They said: We suspect ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah.
He summoned him, was angry with him, and said: “Why does one of you kill his brother? Why did you not invoke a blessing? Wash for him.”
So he washed his face, his hands, his elbows, his knees, the ends of his feet, and the inside of his waist-wrapper in a cup, then it was poured over him, and Sahl went off with the people with nothing wrong with him (2) .
أبو صالح: حدثني أبو شريح، أنه سمع سهل بن أبي أمامة بن سهل يحدث عن أبيه، عن جده:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not be harsh upon yourselves, for those before you were destroyed only by their harshness upon themselves, and you will find ⟦2:326⟧ their remnants in the monasteries and convents (1)” .
إسماعيل بن أبي خالد: عن عامر، عن عبد الله بن معقل، قال:
ʿAlī prayed over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf and pronounced the takbīr six times (2) .
Narrated by: الأعمش، عن يزيد، عن ابن معقل, who said:
He pronounced the takbīr five times, then turned to us and said: He is a Badrī (البدري) (3) . ⟦2:327⟧
Ibn Saʿd said: Sahl ibn Ḥunayf ibn Wāhib ibn ʿUkaym ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Mujdaʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥanash ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, Abū Saʿd and Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
His children were: Abū Umāmah Asʿad, ʿUthmān, and Saʿd, and his descendants today are in Medina and in Baghdad.
He said: They said: The Prophet ﷺ paired Sahl with ʿAlī as brothers.
He witnessed Badr, stood firm on the day of Uḥud, pledged allegiance unto death, and kept shooting arrows in defence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Provide Sahl with arrows, for he is amenable” (1) .
al-Zuhrī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave none of the Anṣār any of the wealth of Banū al-Naḍīr except Sahl ibn Ḥunayf and Abū Dujānah, as they were both poor.
الأعمش: عن يزيد بن زياد - مدني - عن عبد الله بن معقل، قال:
ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), throughout his rule, pronounced four takbīrs over every funeral, except over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, over whom he pronounced five, then turned to them and said: He is a Badrī (البدري) (2) . ⟦2:328⟧
أبو نعيم: حدثنا أبو جناب، سمعت عمير بن سعيد يقول:
ʿAlī prayed over Sahl and pronounced the takbīr five times.
They said: What is this?
He said: The people of Badr have a merit over others, so I wished to let you know his merit (1) .
عمرو بن دينار: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال:
ʿAlī entered with his sword to Fāṭimah as she was washing the blood from the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: Take it, for I fought well with it.
The Prophet ﷺ said: “If you have fought well, then Sahl ibn Ḥunayf has fought well too (2)” .
A similar report is narrated as mursal (مرسل).

159.h: 64 - Khawwāt ibn Jubayr ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Umayyah ibn al-Burak al-Anṣārī * (بخ)
159.t:
He is Imruʾ al-Qays ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf al-Anṣārī, al-Awsī. ⟦2:329⟧
Brother of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr al-ʿAqabī, the Badrī (البدري), who was the commander of the archers on the day of Uḥud.
Khawwāt's patronymic (الكنية) was Abū Ṣāliḥ.
Qays ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah said: His patronymic (الكنية) was Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
Ibn Saʿd said: They said: Khawwāt ibn Jubayr was the owner of the two butter-skins (1) in the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية), then he embraced Islam and his Islam was good (2) .
al-Wāqidī: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān informed me, from Khawwāt ibn Ṣāliḥ, from his father.
And Ibn Abī Sabrah informed us, from al-Miswar ibn Rifāʿah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mukannif:
that Khawwāt ibn Jubayr set out for Badr, and when he was at al-Rawḥāʾ a sharp stone fragment struck him and he was injured, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him back to Medina and allotted him his share and reward, so he was like one who had witnessed it (3) .
They said: Khawwāt died in Medina in the year 40, aged 74; he used to dye his hair, and he was of medium height (4) . ⟦2:330⟧

160.h: 65 - His brother: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Umayyah al-Anṣārī *
160.t:
He witnessed: al-ʿAqabah with the seventy, and Badr, and Uḥud.
On that day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him over the archers, who were fifty men, and commanded them, and they stood at ʿAynayn (1) ; he was martyred that day and was mutilated.
ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl killed him (2) .

161.h: 66 - Qatādah ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Zayd ibn ʿĀmir al-Anṣārī ** (ع)
161.t:
The commander, the fighter in the cause of Allah, Abū ʿUmar al-Anṣārī, al-Ẓafarī, the Badrī (البدري). ⟦2:331⟧
One of the noble Companions (الصحابي), and he was the maternal brother of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī.
He is the one whose eye fell upon his cheek on the day of Uḥud, and it was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pressed it with his noble hand and put it back, and it became the healthier of his two eyes (1) .
He has some hadiths.
Narrating from him: his brother; Abū Saʿīd, and his son; ʿUmar, and Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, and others.
He was in the vanguard of the Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين) ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb when he marched to Syria, and he was one of the renowned archers. ⟦2:332⟧
He lived 65 years.
He died in the year 23 AH, in Medina, and ʿUmar descended into his grave that day.
عبد الرحمن بن الغسيل: حدثنا عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة، عن أبيه، عن جده:
that his eye was hit on the day of Badr, and his eyeball ran down onto his cheek, so the men wanted to cut it off, but they said: Let us go to the Prophet of Allah and consult him.
So he came and told him what had happened.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew him near, raised his eyeball until he placed it back in its place, then pressed it with his palm and said: “O Allah, clothe him with beauty.”
He died, and whoever met him did not know which of his eyes had been hit (1) ?!
Ibn Saʿd said: Banū Ẓafar are from the Aws.
It is said: his patronymic (الكنية) was Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
al-Wāqidī said: He witnessed al-ʿAqabah with the seventy.
Ibn ʿUqbah and Abū Maʿshar said likewise.
Ibn Isḥāq did not mention him among those who witnessed al-ʿAqabah (may Allah be pleased with him).

162.h: 67 - ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAnazī * (ع)
162.t:
ʿAnz ibn Wāʾil.
One of the allies of the family of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb al-ʿAdawī. ⟦2:333⟧
One of the first forerunners.
He embraced Islam before ʿUmar, emigrated both emigrations, and witnessed Badr.
Ibn Isḥāq said: The first to arrive in Medina as an emigrant was Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, and after him ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah (1) .
He has some hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ and from Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
Narrating from him: his son; ʿAbd Allāh, and Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn al-Zubayr, and Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl, and others.
al-Khaṭṭāb had adopted him, and he carried the banner of ʿUmar when he arrived at al-Jābiyah (2) .
al-Wāqidī said: ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah died a few days after the killing of ʿUthmān; he had kept to his house, and the people were unaware until his funeral procession was brought out (3) .
He narrated: يحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري، عن عبد الله بن عامر بن ربيعة:
that his father was seen in a dream when they were attacking ʿUthmān, and it was said to him: Rise and ask Allah to protect you from strife.
ʿĀmir died: in the year fifty and thirty, a short time before the murder of ʿUthmān.
جعفر بن عون: أخبرنا يحيى بن سعيد، عن عبد الله بن عامر بن ⟦2:334⟧ ربيعة، قال:
When they attacked ʿUthmān, my father prayed in the night and supplicated, saying: O Allah, protect me from strife, with that by which You protected the righteous among Your servants.
Then he did not go out, and he entered the morning only as a funeral procession (1) .
